proposals.definition: A lotus plant, or a cluster or pond of lotuses (Sanskrit kamalinī, from kamala, 'lotus'). In song 27 (3b) the kamalinī carries the lotus along a conduit. Munidatta explains the word as 'she who has the lotus juice', the juice of great bliss (cp.27.m4); the Tibetan has pad+ma can, 'the one with the lotus'.
proposals.symbolicImage: the lotus plant (kamalinī) that carries the lotus along the conduit

symbolicReadings.referent: the naturally purified avadhūtikā, Nairātmā, so called because she has the lotus juice, the juice of great bliss; with that juice, bodhicitta, she gladdens the vajra of body and carries it to the region of the wheel of great bliss

proposals.rationale: A new image of the twilight language that Munidatta reads as the purified avadhūtī; 'lotus plant' keeps the image and keeps it apart from the lotus (kamala) it carries in the same line and from the lotus grove (nalinīvana).

proposals.definition: A conduit or channel for water, a spout or drain (Old Bengali paṇāla, Sanskrit praṇāla, praṇālī). In song 27 (3b) the lotus plant carries the lotus 'by the conduit' (paṇālem̐). Munidatta does not gloss the word; the Tibetan line has 'bab pa'i chu, 'flowing water', perhaps for it.
proposals.rationale: A rare concrete image in the verse; 'conduit' gives the water-channel sense and keeps it apart from 'channel', the glossary's rendering of the subtle-body nāḍī.

proposals.definition: The peak or summit (śikhara) of the vajra. Munidatta says the moon of bodhicitta, moving by the path of the avadhūtī, reaches the vajra peak, and at its tip goes to nirvāṇa, clear light (cp.27.m3, cp.27.m4); the Tibetan has rdo rje'i rtse mo. He does not say here where in the body it lies.
proposals.rationale: Munidatta's name for the place the moon reaches in this song; a fixed rendering keeps it apart from the vajra itself and from the summit of Sumeru.

proposals.definition: A sandhyā is a juncture of the day, such as dawn or dusk, at which rites are performed. Munidatta sets the wisdom-knowledge empowerment 'at midnight, at the fourth juncture' (cp.27.m2), naming the two together. The Tibetan has nam phyed kyi thun mtshams bzhi, which could also mean 'the four junctures of midnight'.
proposals.rationale: Munidatta's time-word for the midnight empowerment, already named in the midnight entry (whose forbidden list includes 'fourth juncture'); one rendering keeps it consistent wherever it recurs.

proposals.definition: A 'chapter on empowerment' (seka, 'consecration, empowerment'; paṭala, 'chapter'), whose prescribed rite Munidatta follows when he sets the empowerment at midnight (cp.27.m2); the Tibetan has dbang gi le'u. He does not say which tantra's chapter he means, and the phrase may describe a chapter rather than give a title.
proposals.rationale: Munidatta cites it as his authority for the midnight empowerment; readers need to know it is a chapter of an unnamed tantra, not a known separate work.

proposals.definition: Meeting, union (Old Bengali mela; Sanskrit melā, melaka). In the last couplet of song 27 Bhusuku says he understood 'in union' (melem̐). Munidatta renders it melaka, in 'the union of wisdom and means' (cp.27.m6); the Tibetan line has tshogs pa, 'gathering, assembly', and the Tibetan comment sbyor ba, 'joining'.
proposals.symbolicImage: the union (melem̐) in which Bhusuku says he understood

symbolicReadings.referent: the union of wisdom and means (prajñopāyamelaka), in which Bhusuku, by the true guru's grace, playfully understood innate joy, great bliss

proposals.rationale: The key word of Bhusuku's signature couplet, which Munidatta and the Tibetan read differently; a plain 'union' keeps the line open and the entry records both readings.

proposals.definition: Teacher whom Munidatta quotes at the end of his comment on song 27, for a verse beginning gavāṃ yūtha, 'a herd of cows' (cp.27.m5). The Tibetan translation names him rdo rje Da DI zhabs, which suggests a name like Ḍaḍī. Possibly the same teacher as Daṛatīpāda, quoted on song 11; not otherwise identified here.
proposals.rationale: A named authority in the commentary; kept apart from Daṛatīpāda (p-darati) until the reviewer decides whether the two names are one.

proposals.definition: Midnight. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali adharāti (1a); in Munidatta's comment, arddharātrau and the quoted adharātī (m2).
proposals.rationale: Adds the short-i spelling of the song, the plain Sanskrit locative and the commentary's citation of the verse word, which the existing forms (adharātī as Old Bengali, punararddharātrau) do not match in the Sanskrit.

proposals.definition: A woman practitioner of yoga. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali joiṇī (1b) and Munidatta's yoginī (m2).
proposals.rationale: Adds the retroflex, long-ī spelling of the song (the entry has only joini) and the plain Sanskrit yoginī, which no existing form matches on its own.

proposals.definition: The moon. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali ṣaṣahara (2a, 3a), Munidatta's śaśaharo (m4) and candraḥ (m3), Tibetan ri bong 'dzin (2a).
proposals.rationale: Adds the ṣ-spelling of śaśahara used twice in the song, the commentary's śaśaharo and sasahara-…-candraḥ (the existing sasahara is listed for the verse only), and the Tibetan ri bong 'dzin without the particle pa.

proposals.definition: The central channel. Song 27 form: Old Bengali abadhūi (2a), avadhūtī with the t dropped.
proposals.rationale: Adds the song's Apabhraṃśa-style spelling, which none of the existing forms matches; the Tibetan line has a wa d+hU tIr.

proposals.definition: Path. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali māge, 'on the path' (2a), and Munidatta's avadhūtīmārgeṇa (m3, m4).
proposals.rationale: Adds the song's own word for the path (Tibetan lam) and the instrumental mārgeṇa; māge is given as a form only, without a match, because Bengali māge is also 'asks, begs'.

proposals.definition: The innate. Song 27 form: Old Bengali ṣahaje (2b).
proposals.rationale: Adds the ṣ-spelling of the refrain, which the existing sahaje does not match.

proposals.definition: Jewel. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali raaṇahu (2b) and Munidatta's tattvaratna (m3).
proposals.rationale: Adds the inflected raaṇahu, whose full form also outranks anahata's aṇaha, which otherwise sits inside it, and Munidatta's plain ratna in 'the jewel of the reality of the true guru's word'.

proposals.definition: Nirvāṇa. Song 27 form: Old Bengali ṇibāṇem̐ (3a).
proposals.rationale: Adds the song's spelling with initial ṇ and final ṇ, which neither nibāṇe nor ṇibānā matches.

proposals.definition: Beyond characteristics. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali bilakṣaṇa (4a) and Munidatta's vilakṣaṇa (m5).
proposals.rationale: The entry's only matchable Bengali form is the compound yasmin vilakṣaṇasamaye (its other forms carry 'Beng' instead of the source text), so the bare word in the song and the commentary is not yet recognised.

proposals.definition: Awakened one. Song 27 form: Old Bengali budha (4b), which the Tibetan renders sangs rgyas.
proposals.rationale: Adds budha, read as buddha with the double consonant simplified (as sudha for śuddha in 4a) and as the Tibetan sangs rgyas reads it; matched as a whole word only, since budha can also mean 'wise'.

proposals.definition: Innate joy. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali sahajānanda (5b) and Munidatta's sahajānandarasapūrṇo (m1).
proposals.rationale: Adds the bare stem, which the entry lacks (it has only sahajānandena and sahajānandaṃ); at present the bare form falls to the general entry for joy.

proposals.definition: Play. Song 27 forms: Old Bengali lolem̐ (5b), which Munidatta renders līlayā, 'in play' (m6), and the Tibetan rol.
proposals.rationale: Adds lolem̐ on the strength of Munidatta's līlayā and the Tibetan rol, and the instrumental līlayā, which the existing forms do not match.

proposals.definition: The wheel of great bliss. Song 27 form: Munidatta's mahāsukhacakroddeśaṃ, 'the region of the wheel of great bliss' (m4).
proposals.rationale: Adds a form the existing literals miss (they end in -cakraṃ or run on to -samudroddeśena).

proposals.definition: Clear light. Song 27 form: Munidatta's prabhāsvaraṃ (m4), in apposition to nirvāṇa.
proposals.rationale: Adds the bare accusative, which none of the existing compound forms matches.

proposals.definition: The uṣṇīṣa. Song 27 form: Munidatta's uṣṇīṣakamalaṃ, 'the uṣṇīṣa lotus' (m2).
proposals.rationale: Adds a form the entry's only Bengali literal (uṣṇīṣakamalamadhumadanaṃ) does not match; the Tibetan gtsug tor is already there.

forms.translit: shes rab ye shes kyi dbang

proposals.definition: Empowerment. Song 27 forms: Munidatta's prajñājñānābhiṣekadānasamaye (m2) and the Tibetan shes rab ye shes kyi dbang.
proposals.rationale: Adds the wisdom-knowledge empowerment as it stands in this comment, so the compound goes to empowerment rather than splitting; the existing literal ends in -ṃ and does not match it.

proposals.definition: The thirty-two marks and eighty signs. Song 27 forms: Munidatta's dvātriṃśallakṣaṇayukto and vyañjanāśītyalaṃkṛtaḥ (m5).
proposals.rationale: Adds the two separate phrases of this comment, which the entry's single long compound does not match.

proposals.definition: Reality. Song 27 forms: Munidatta's anadhigatatattvānām (m5) and sadguruvacanatattva- (m3).
proposals.rationale: Adds two forms that the existing literals (tattvaṃ, tatvonmīli(la)tamātraṃ) miss; the stem tattva with its double t does not occur inside unrelated words here.

proposals.definition: Grace. Song 27 forms: Munidatta's guruprasādād (m5) and sadguruprasādāl (m6).
proposals.rationale: Adds the guru's grace as it stands twice in this comment; the entry's matchable Bengali literal is only gurucaraṇareṇuprasādāt.

proposals.definition: Joy. Song 27 form: Munidatta's ānandādi-, 'joy and the rest' (m2).
proposals.rationale: Adds the bare word, which no existing form matches; with an initial vowel letter it cannot sit inside compounds such as sahajānanda.

proposals.definition: Lotus nectar. Song 27 forms: Munidatta's kamalarasaṃ (m4, twice) and the Tibetan pad+ma'i ro and chu skyes kyi ro for it.
proposals.rationale: Adds the plain Sanskrit accusative, which neither kamalarasa (listed for the verse) nor kamalarasam iti matches in the commentary, and the two Tibetan renderings, which the existing chu skyes khu ba and chu skyes kyi ro'i do not cover.

proposals.definition: The refrain. Song 27 form: the Tibetan b+h+rU'i rkang pa (m3), with bha for dha.
proposals.rationale: Adds the Tibetan's spelling here, which none of the existing Tibetan forms (d+h+rU'i, d+hU'i, d+hA'i rkang pa) matches.

proposals.definition: The joy of cessation. Song 27 form: Old Bengali biramānanda (4a).
proposals.rationale: The entry's forms are all Sanskrit (commentary) or Tibetan, so the word in the verse itself is not recognised; this adds it for the Old Bengali.

proposals.definition: The lotus. Song 27 form: Munidatta's kamalaṃ (m2), glossed as the uṣṇīṣa lotus.
proposals.rationale: The entry's kamala is listed for the verse only, and none of its Sanskrit forms matches the bare kamalaṃ of the commentary.

proposals.definition: A spiritual teacher. Song 27 forms: Munidatta's sadguru- (m3) and guru- (m5) in compounds.
proposals.rationale: The entry's guru and sadguru are listed for the verse only and its Sanskrit forms are inflected (sadguroḥ, gurau), so the stem in the commentary's five compounds is not recognised.

proposals.definition: Bhusukupāda, the poet of song 27. Song 27 form: Munidatta's bhusukusiddhācāryyaḥ (m1).
proposals.rationale: Adds the name without -pāda as it stands in Munidatta's opening line; the entry's bare bhusuku is listed for the verse only.

questions: Thirty-two yoginīs: I was told this entry exists, but the glossary in this pack has none (nothing carries বতিস জোইণী, cp.27.1b), so I have only added জোইণী to yogini. If the entry exists outside the pack, it should take বতিস জোইণী as a form. If it does not, it deserves one: Munidatta reads the thirty-two yoginīs as the thirty-two channels that carry bodhicitta (cp.27.m2), and the Tibetan agrees.

Shadowing in ananda: the general 'joy' entry lists the Sanskrit forms সহজানন্দ, বিরমানন্দে and চতুর্থানন্দ. In m1, সহজানন্দ now ties with my new sahajananda form. In m5, বিরমানন্দেত্যাদি goes to ananda, because বিরমানন্দে is longer than viramananda's বিরমানন্দ. I suggest moving those forms to sahajananda, viramananda and a fourth-joy entry.

Overlap: anahata's Old Bengali অণহ sits inside রঅণহু, 'jewels' (2b). My new ratna form রঅণহু is longer and so outranks it here. A whole-word regex for অণহ would stop the same thing happening elsewhere.

Coverage across languages: matching is per language, and many existing forms are listed only for the verse (oben) or only for the commentary (san). Several of my 'new forms' (viramananda, lotus, guru, p-bhusuku, moon, kamala-rasa, ardharatri) are there so that the same word is recognised on the other side. If the live match lists already hold these strings for that language, the merge simply ignores the duplicates.

বুধ (4b) is filed under buddha, matched as a whole word only. The Tibetan reads sangs rgyas, Munidatta identifies the knower with the Blessed Vajradhara (m5), and the line before has সুধ for śuddha. But budha, 'wise one', is possible: drop the form if you prefer 'wise'.

লোলেঁ (5b) is filed under lila ('play') because Munidatta renders it līlayā (m6) and the Tibetan has rol. Etymologically it looks like lola, 'tremulous, eager'. Split it out if you want the song's word kept apart from the gloss.
মাগে (2a, 'on the path'; Tibetan lam) is added to marga as a form with no match, because Bengali māge also means 'asks, begs'.

Davaṛīpāda (m5; Tibetan rdo rje Da DI zhabs) is proposed separately as p-davari. The existing Daṛatīpāda (p-darati, song 11) has the Tibetan da u Da'i zhabs, which fits a name like Davaḍa, close to Davaṛī. They may be one teacher: merge if you agree.

kamalinī: I chose 'lotus plant' (translate) over keep-source 'kamalinī'. Munidatta's etymology ('she who has the lotus juice', m4) and the Tibetan pad+ma can both depend on the possessive sense, which no English rendering keeps.
tx-sekapatala: Munidatta's sekapaṭala (m2; Tibetan dbang gi le'u) may describe the empowerment chapter of some tantra rather than give a title. Recast it as a term if it never recurs as a name.
Not proposed, for the drafters: abhedyā and sūkṣmarūpā (m2; Tibetan mi phyed ma, phra mo'i gzugs) look like the names of particular channels from a list of the thirty-two, not plain adjectives.

Data glitch: some existing forms have 'Beng' or 'Tibt' in the script field where the source text should be (vilaksana, pada, prasada, samaya, abhasa), so those forms can never match. That is why vilaksana and prasada needed new forms here.
